the energy transfer function is universal and that the luminescence efficiency of a phosphor is proportional to the energy transfer function times a material characteristic constant.

the luminescence efficiency of a thin screen is determined by a universal energy transfer function which is independent of the phosphor material and that, in the energy range of interest, this energy transfer function can be approximated by the sum of two exponentials.
the energy yield of luminescence is proportional to the energy transfer function, and this function is universal for all thin phosphors and all X-ray or gamma-ray energies.

the development of a theoretical framework that can be used to calculate luminescence yields in X-ray phosphors.
the development of a theory to explain the luminescence efficiency in roentgenography with high-energy X-rays.
the development of an improved X-ray luminescence technique for use in roentgenography.

the energy dependence of the X-ray luminescence yield of thin phosphors is essentially the same for all materials, but the absolute yield is different and depends strongly upon the material.

the luminescence of a phosphor is determined by the energy transfer function, which depends only on the energy of the incident radiation and on the atomic number of the target material, and by the energy escape function, which depends on the atomic number and density of the phosphor.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the energy transfer function for luminescent screen absorption is universal, and that the energy escape function for luminescence is also universal for all materials except the light elements, and that for the light elements the energy escape function can be estimated from the known energy escape function for the light elements.
the energy transfer function is the dominant factor in determining the yield of phosphors for X-ray or gamma ray excitation.
a single universal energy transfer function, with a single energy escape function, is adequate to describe the luminescence of all phosphors for all energies of X-rays and gamma rays in thin screens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy transfer function is a universal function for thin phosphor screens.
the luminescence efficiency of a thin phosphor is independent of the energy of incident radiation.
the luminescence efficiency of a thin luminescent screen is independent of the incident energy, as long as the electron escape is negligible.
